raw_answer_text:
A1: It is broadcast to every station on the Ethernet segment (broadcast MAC address), since the sender doesn't know which specific station holds the target.
A2: It lacks the mapping between the target's IP (protocol) address and its Ethernet (hardware) address in its ARP cache/table.
A3: It stores the requesting host's protocol (IP) address paired with its hardware (MAC) address.
A4: No, hosts that are not the target simply discard the request without replying.
A5: The reply is sent directly (unicast) to the requesting host, not broadcast.
A6: The requesting host stores the target's protocol/hardware address pair in its own ARP table (cache), completing the resolution so it can now send the intended packet.
A7: The requesting host does not know the target's hardware address; obtaining that address is exactly the purpose of the request.
A8: Per RFC 826 procedure, a host merges the sender's address mapping into its table first, and only afterward checks the opcode to decide whether to also send a reply.
